readings.title: The Premial System of Repayment
readings.subtitle: Laws of Theft, Damage, and Borrowing
readings.text: [Exodus 22:1] <dq>“When a man steals an ox or a sheep, and shall slaughter it or sell it, he repays five cattle for an ox and four sheep for a sheep.</dq> [2] <dq>“If the thief is found breaking in, and he is struck so that he dies, there is no guilt for his bloodshed.</dq> [3] <dq>“If the sun has risen on him, there is guilt for his bloodshed, he shall certainly repay. If he has not the means, then he shall be sold for his theft.</dq> [4] <dq>“If the theft is indeed found alive in his hand, whether it is an ox or donkey or sheep, he repays double.</dq> [5] <dq>“When a man lets a field or vineyard be grazed bare, and lets loose <dn>את</dn> his livestock, and it feeds in another man’s field, he repays from the best of his own field and the best of his own vineyard.</dq> [6] <dq>“When fire breaks out and spreads to thorn bushes, so that stacked grain, or standing grain, or the field is consumed, he who kindled <dn>את</dn> the fire shall certainly repay.</dq> [7] <dq>“When a man gives silver or goods to his neighbour to guard, and it is stolen out of the man’s house, if the thief is found, he repays double.</dq> [8] <dq>“If the thief is not found, then the master of the house shall be brought before <dn>Elohim</dn> to see whether he has put his hand into his neighbour’s goods.</dq> [9] <dq>“For every matter of transgression, for ox, for donkey, for sheep, for garment, or for whatever is lost which another claims to be his, let the matter of them both come before <dn>Elohim</dn>. And whomever <dn>Elohim</dn> declares wrong repays double to his neighbour.</dq> [10] <dq>“When a man gives to his neighbour a donkey, or ox, or sheep, or any beast to watch over, and it dies, or is injured, or is driven away while no one is looking,</dq> [11] <dq>let an oath of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> be between them both, that he has not put his hand into his neighbour’s goods. And the owner of it shall accept that, and he does not repay.</dq> [12] <dq>“But if it is indeed stolen from him, he repays to its owner.</dq> [13] <dq>“If it is torn to pieces, then let him bring it for evidence, he does not repay what was torn.</dq> [14] <dq>“And when a man borrows from his neighbour, and it is injured or dies while the owner of it is not present, he shall certainly repay.</dq> [15] <dq>“But if its owner was with it, he does not repay. If it was hired, he is entitled to the hire.</dq>

readings.title: Laws of Purity and Compassion
readings.subtitle: Protecting the Vulnerable and Honoring the Creator
readings.text: [Exodus 22:16] <dq>“And when a man entices a maiden who is not engaged, and lies with her, he shall certainly pay the bride-price for her to be his wife.</dq> [17] <dq>“If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, he pays according to the bride-price of maidens.</dq> [18] <dq>“Do not allow a practiser of witchcraft to live.</dq> [19] <dq>“Anyone lying with a beast shall certainly be put to death.</dq> [20] <dq>“He who slaughters to an elohim, except to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> only, is put under the ban.</dq> [21] <dq>“Do not tread down a sojourner or oppress him, for you were sojourners in the land of Mitsrayim.</dq> [22] <dq>“Do not afflict any widow or fatherless child.</dq> [23] <dq>“If you do afflict them at all – if they cry out to <dn>Me</dn> at all, <dn>I</dn> shall certainly hear their cry,</dq> [24] <dq>and <dn>My</dn> wrath shall burn and <dn>I</dn> shall kill <dn>את</dn> you with the sword, your wives shall be widows and your children fatherless.</dq> [25] <dq>“If you do lend silver to <dn>את</dn> any of <dn>My</dn> people, <dn>את</dn> the poor among you, you are not to be like one that lends on interest to him. Do not lay interest on him.</dq> [26] <dq>“If you take your neighbour’s garment as a pledge at all, you are to return it to him before the sun goes down.</dq> [27] <dq>“For that is his only covering, it is his garment for his skin. What does he sleep in? And it shall be that when he cries to <dn>Me</dn>, <dn>I</dn> shall hear, for <dn>I</dn> show favour.</dq> [28] <dq>“Do not revile an elohim, nor curse a ruler of your people.</dq> [29] <dq>“Do not delay giving your harvest and your vintage. Give <dn>Me</dn> the first-born of your sons.</dq> [30] <dq>“Likewise you are to do with your oxen, with your sheep. It is to be with its mother seven days. On the eighth day you give it to <dn>Me</dn>.</dq> [31] <dq>“And you are set-apart men to <dn>Me</dn>, and you do not eat any meat which is torn to pieces in the field, you throw it to the dogs.</dq>

readings.title: Righteousness in Judgment
readings.subtitle: The Sabbath Rest for the Land and the Beast
readings.text: [Exodus 23:1] <dq>“Do not bring <dn>את</dn> a false report. Do not put your hand with the wrong to be a malicious witness.</dq> [2] <dq>“Do not follow a crowd to do evil, nor bear witness in a strife so as to turn aside after many, to turn aside what is right.</dq> [3] <dq>“And do not favour a poor man in his strife.</dq> [4] <dq>“When you meet your enemy’s ox or his donkey going astray, you shall certainly return it to him.</dq> [5] <dq>“When you see the donkey of him who hates you lying under its burden, you shall refrain from leaving it to him, you shall certainly help him.</dq> [6] <dq>“Do not turn aside the right-ruling of your poor in his strife.</dq> [7] <dq>“Keep yourself far from a false matter, and do not kill the innocent and the righteous, for <dn>I</dn> do not declare the wrong right.</dq> [8] <dq>“And do not take a bribe, for a bribe blinds the seeing one and twists the words of the righteous.</dq> [9] <dq>“And do not oppress a sojourner, as you yourselves know <dn>את</dn> the heart of a sojourner, because you were sojourners in the land of Mitsrayim.</dq> [10] <dq>“And for six years you are to sow <dn>את</dn> your land, and shall gather <dn>את</dn> its increase,</dq> [11] <dq>but the seventh year you are to let it rest, and shall leave it, and the poor of your people shall eat. And what they leave, the beasts of the field eat. Do the same with your vineyard and your oliveyard.</dq> [12] <dq>“Six days you are to do your work, and on the seventh day you rest, in order that your ox and your donkey might rest, and the son of your female servant and the sojourner be refreshed.</dq> [13] <dq>“And in all that <dn>I</dn> have said to you take heed. And make no mention of the name of other mighty ones, let it not be heard from your mouth.</dq>

readings.title: The Three Pilgrimage Festivals
readings.subtitle: Matzot, Harvest, and Ingathering
readings.text: [Exodus 23:14] <dq>“Three times in the year you are to celebrate a festival to <dn>Me</dn>:</dq> [15] <dq>“Guard <dn>את</dn> the Festival of Matzot. Seven days you eat unleavened bread, as <dn>I</dn> commanded you, at the time appointed in the new moon of Aḇiḇ – for in it you came out of Mitsrayim – and do not appear before <dn>Me</dn> empty-handed;</dq> [16] <dq>and the Festival of the Harvest, the first-fruits of your labours which you have sown in the field; and the Festival of the Ingathering at the outgoing of the year, when you have gathered in <dn>את</dn> the fruit of your labours from the field.</dq> [17] <dq>“Three times in the year all your males are to appear before <dn>את</dn> the Master <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [18] <dq>“Do not slaughter the blood of <dn>My</dn> slaughtering with leavened bread, and the fat of <dn>My</dn> festival shall not remain until morning.</dq> [19] <dq>“Bring <dn>את</dn> the first of the first-fruits of your land into the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. Do not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.</dq>

readings.title: The Messenger of the Covenant
readings.subtitle: Conquest and Separation from Pagan Mighty Ones
readings.text: [Exodus 23:20] <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am sending a Messenger before you to guard you in the way and to bring you into the place which <dn>I</dn> have prepared.</dq> [21] <dq>“Be on guard before <dn>Him</dn> and obey <dn>His</dn> voice. Do not rebel against <dn>Him</dn>, for <dn>He</dn> is not going to pardon your transgression, for <dn>My</dn> Name is in <dn>Him</dn>.</dq> [22] <dq>“But if you diligently obey <dn>His</dn> voice and shall do all that <dn>I</dn> speak, then <dn>I</dn> shall be an enemy to <dn>את</dn> your enemies and a distresser to <dn>את</dn> those who distress you.</dq> [23] <dq>“For <dn>My</dn> Messenger shall go before you and shall bring you in to the Amorites and the Ḥittites and the Perizzites and the Kena‛anites and the Ḥivvites and the Yeḇusites, and <dn>I</dn> shall cut them off.</dq> [24] <dq>“Do not bow down to their mighty ones, nor serve them, nor do according to their works, but without fail overthrow them and without fail break down their pillars.</dq> [25] <dq>“And you shall serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> shall bless <dn>את</dn> your bread and <dn>את</dn> your water. And <dn>I</dn> shall remove sickness from your midst.</dq> [26] <dq>“None shall miscarry or be barren in your land. <dn>I</dn> shall fill <dn>את</dn> the number of your days.</dq> [27] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall send <dn>My</dn> fear before you, and cause confusion among <dn>את</dn> all the people to whom you come, and make <dn>את</dn> all your enemies turn their backs to you.</dq> [28] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall send <dn>את</dn> hornets before you, which shall drive out <dn>את</dn> the Ḥivvite, <dn>את</dn> the Kena‛anite, and <dn>את</dn> the Ḥittite from before you.</dq> [29] <dq>“<dn>I</dn> shall not drive them out from before you in one year, lest the land become a waste and the beast of the field become too numerous for you.</dq> [30] <dq>“Little by little <dn>I</dn> shall drive them out from before you, until you have increased, and you inherit <dn>את</dn> the land.</dq> [31] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall set <dn>את</dn> your border from the Sea of Reeds to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River, for <dn>I</dn> shall give the inhabitants of the land into your hand, and you shall drive them out before you.</dq> [32] <dq>“Do not make a covenant with them nor with their mighty ones.</dq> [33] <dq>“Let them not dwell in your land, lest they make <dn>את</dn> you sin against <dn>Me</dn> when you serve <dn>את</dn> their mighty ones, when it becomes a snare to you.”</dq>

readings.title: The Seventy Elders See Elohim
readings.subtitle: Mosheh Ascends the Mountain of Fire
readings.text: [Exodus 24:1] And to Mosheh <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Come up to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, you and Aharon, Naḏaḇ and Aḇihu, and seventy of the elders of Yisra’ěl, and you shall bow yourselves from a distance.</dq> [2] <dq>“But Mosheh shall draw near to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> by himself, and let them not draw near, nor let the people go up with him.”</dq> [3] And Mosheh came and related to the people <dn>את</dn> all the Words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>את</dn> all the right-rulings. And all the people answered with one voice and said, “All the Words which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken we shall do.” [4] And Mosheh wrote down <dn>את</dn> all the Words of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and rose up early in the morning, and built a slaughter-place at the foot of the mountain, and twelve standing columns for the twelve tribes of Yisra’ěl. [5] And he sent <dn>את</dn> young men of the children of Yisra’ěl, and they offered ascending offerings and slaughtered slaughterings of peace offerings to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of bulls. [6] And Mosheh took <dn>את</dn> half the blood and put it in basins, and half the blood he sprinkled on the slaughter-place. [7] And he took the Book of the Covenant and read in the hearing of the people. And they said, “All that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken we shall do, and obey.” [8] And Mosheh took <dn>את</dn> the blood and sprinkled it on the people, and said, “See, the blood of the covenant which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has made with you concerning all these Words.” [9] And Mosheh went up, also Aharon, Naḏaḇ, and Aḇihu, and seventy of the elders of Yisra’ěl, [10] and they saw <dn>את</dn> the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, and under <dn>His</dn> feet like a paved work of sapphire stone, and like the heavens for brightness. [11] Yet <dn>He</dn> did not stretch out <dn>His</dn> hand against the chiefs of the children of Yisra’ěl! And they saw <dn>את</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, and they ate and drank. [12] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Come up to <dn>Me</dn> on the mountain and be there, while <dn>I</dn> give you <dn>את</dn> tablets of stone, and the Torah and the command which <dn>I</dn> have written, to teach them.”</dq> [13] And Mosheh arose with his assistant Yehoshua, and Mosheh went up to the mountain of <dn>Elohim</dn>. [14] And he said to the elders, “Wait here for us until we come back to you. And see, Aharon and Ḥur are with you. Whoever has matters, let him go to them.” [15] And Mosheh went up into the mountain, and a cloud covered <dn>את</dn> the mountain. [16] And the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> dwelt on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. And on the seventh day <dn>He</dn> called to Mosheh out of the midst of the cloud. [17] And the appearance of the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was like a consuming fire on the top of the mountain, before the eyes of the children of Yisra’ěl. [18] And Mosheh went into the midst of the cloud and went up into the mountain. And it came to be that Mosheh was on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
